audit_findings.title: The valuation treats all bridge cash as excess despite operating-liquidity needs
audit_findings.mechanism: Any cash required for inventory funding, seasonal working capital, or covenant support must be excluded from the cash bridge, reducing equity value dollar-for-dollar.
audit_findings.evidence: We must maintain and have adequate working capital to purchase sufficient inventory to meet customer demand.
audit_findings.explanation: The valuation demonstrably adds the entire $318.178 million cash balance, which exceeds each scenario's resulting equity value because operating value is negative. The filing establishes that working capital is operationally necessary, but it does not quantify minimum required cash. The $336.8 million available revolver and covenant compliance reduce immediate liquidity concern but do not establish that every dollar of cash is distributable. The potential overstatement is therefore real but its materiality cannot be measured from the record.
audit_findings.action: Determine unrestricted excess cash using seasonal cash lows, inventory funding needs, borrowing-base availability, covenant liquidity requirements, and management's minimum operating-cash policy as of July 4, 2026; rerun the bridge with only excess cash.

audit_findings.title: Lease-funded fleet replacement may be missing from reinvestment
audit_findings.magnitude: $44.564 million in fiscal 2025, $19.373 million in fiscal 2024, and $19.861 million in fiscal 2023 of finance-lease asset additions; maintenance portion unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: If depreciation is added back while recurring finance-lease asset additions are omitted from maintenance investment, owner earnings and the terminal earnings base are overstated.
audit_findings.evidence: During fiscal 2025, 2024 and 2023, the Company added fleet assets under finance leases of $ 44.6 million, $ 19.4 million and $ 19.9 million, respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: The noncash additions are filed amounts and fiscal 2025 additions alone equal 340% of the absolute $13.1 million anchor and exceeded the $26.933 million of cash property investment. This establishes material capacity if the additions were omitted, although the supplied record does not demonstrate the valuation's maintenance-capex calculation or establish what portion represented replacement rather than growth.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile each historical OE calculation to cash capital expenditures plus finance-lease additions, classify replacement versus growth spending, and rerun all scenarios and the terminal period with recurring lease-funded maintenance investment included exactly once.

audit_findings.title: The anchor contains only a partial-year contribution from the acquired business
audit_findings.mechanism: A pre-acquisition or partial-period OE numerator applied to the post-acquisition company creates a perimeter mismatch in the anchor and projected operating value.
audit_findings.evidence: Disdero’s results of operations and cash flows are included in the Company’s consolidated financial results beginning at the start of business on November 1, 2025.
audit_findings.explanation: The mismatch is demonstrated: Disdero entered consolidated results only on November 1, 2025, while the bridge reflects the post-acquisition company. Its two-month contribution was only 0.4% of fiscal-2025 net sales, but the business represented 6.4% of year-end assets and ultimately cost $94.351 million. No separate Disdero earnings, working-capital, maintenance-investment, or integration-cost data are supplied, so neither the direction nor materiality of a full-period adjustment can be established.
audit_findings.action: Build a same-perimeter trailing-twelve-month or filed pro-forma OE calculation through July 4, 2026, separately identifying Disdero operating earnings, working-capital requirements, maintenance investment, incremental amortization, and nonrecurring integration costs; then rerun the valuation.

audit_findings.title: Noncash sale-leaseback gains may be capitalized in owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: $3.934 million annually, including $1.967 million in the first six months of 2026; annual amount equals 30.0% of the absolute $13.1 million anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: Unreversed deferred-gain recognition raises the OE anchor without current cash and would be propagated through forecast growth and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: During fiscal 2025, 2024 and 2023, the Company recognized $ 3.9 million, $ 3.9 million, $ 3.9 million, respectively, of these deferred gains.
audit_findings.explanation: The recurring noncash credit and its scale are demonstrated, but inclusion in OE is not: the filed cash-flow statements reverse the gain, while the supplied valuation lacks an OE reconciliation. If the valuation used that cash-flow adjustment, no error exists; if it retained the accounting gain, the amount is material relative to the negative anchor and would overstate value.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the anchor from net income to OE and confirm a full reversal of deferred-gain recognition in every historical year and forecast year; if absent, remove it and rerun all scenarios and terminal value.

audit_findings.title: An accrued import-duty payment may remain ahead of common equity
audit_findings.magnitude: $8.0 million, or $0.94 per fully diluted share
audit_findings.mechanism: Because the related expense was recognized previously but the cash payment remained outstanding, the unpaid obligation reduces cash attributable to common equity through the bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: As of January 3, 2026, the Company estimates that it will be required to pay approximately $ 8.0 million, excluding any interest.
audit_findings.explanation: The latest 10-Q resolves the factual question: the $8.0 million obligation remained accrued in other current liabilities on July 4, 2026, the same date as the $318.178 million cash bridge. Omitting it overstates equity value by $8.0 million before any interest. That equals 4.5% of bear, 5.6% of base, and 7.1% of bull equity value, but only $0.94 per share; correcting it would lower the already far-below-market values of $13.28-$21.08 and cannot close the minimum $60.73 per-share gap to the $81.81 market price.
audit_findings.action: Deduct the $8.0 million accrued duty plus separately verified accrued interest from bridge cash in the next rerun, unless post-July settlement evidence shows the reported cash balance was already reduced.

audit_findings.title: A contingent multiemployer-pension withdrawal claim is outside the ordinary debt treatment
audit_findings.magnitude: $30.4 million contingent complete-withdrawal estimate; approximately $0.7 million of potential annual payments plus approximately $0.6 million of existing annual partial-withdrawal payments
audit_findings.mechanism: A probable withdrawal liability would enter as a probability-weighted claim ahead of common equity or as future cash payments not already captured in OE.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company’s most recent contingent withdrawal liability was estimated at approximately $ 30.4 million for a complete withdrawal occurring in 2025.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing identifies a potentially material exposure equal to $3.59 per fully diluted share and 21.1% of base-case equity value, but no complete or mass withdrawal is reported and the trigger probability is not supplied. It is therefore a forward-looking contingency rather than a demonstrated present valuation error. The existing $6.2 million partial-withdrawal liability and related payments also require reconciliation to avoid either omission or double counting.
audit_findings.action: Monitor plan participation, facility closures, layoffs, collective-bargaining changes, and withdrawal notices; reconcile the existing $6.2 million liability and payments to OE, and introduce a probability-weighted present-value scenario if a complete or mass withdrawal becomes reasonably likely.
